title: Threat Horizons triage workshop - 2026-06-10
agenda: Quick status on open vuln backlog
Threat-modeling sync: private deployments attack surface
Assign mitigations and confirm SLAs for fixes
summary: Half-day workshop to triage three emergent issues from last week: a high-severity dependency RCE candidate, a secrets exposure in test artifacts, and a set of threat-model gaps for private deployments. Goal: prioritize mitigations, assign owners, and confirm short-term controls vs long-term fixes.
discussion_notes:
1) Dependency issue (linalg-utils): Eli walked the group through a reproduction where the library deserializes pickled objects in the CI artifact path. Repro steps pinned to an internal CI job. Library version 2.2.7 accepts crafted input; upstream maintainer acknowledged and proposed a 2.3.1 patch.

We discussed rollback vs patching in place. Marcos flagged that an immediate upgrade may require recompiling some custom kernels — risk to low-latency serving. Consensus: implement an application-level input validation / reject-deserialization guard as a short-term mitigation, then coordinate a staged upgrade of the library in a Canary pool and Dedicated pools after perf regression tests.

2) Secrets scan: Rina shared results from last-night scan: one AWS access key accidentally committed in a test fixture (internal repo redwood-tests). Key had minimal permissions but was used by an automation job. Key has been rotated and credentials revoked. We confirmed no external exposure indicators. Team agreed to: add stricter pre-commit hook on tests repos, enable repository-level block for base64-looking strings in CI, and add test-run environment variable scrubbing in build pipelines.

3) Threat modeling for Private (VPC/on-prem): Priya presented an attack path document enumerating: (A) customer-managed KMS misconfig -> token exfil, (B) misconfigured service mesh allowing lateral movement, (C) exposure of admin control plane endpoints. Actionable suggestion: default private deployments to deny-by-default egress and require explicit KMS usage policy templates and a hardened control-plane bastion template.

Cross-cutting: Jonas emphasized observability gaps — need per-request provenance for model routing decisions and signed audit logs for private control-plane operations. Agreed to track as separate initiative.
decisions: Short-term guard: add deserialization rejection filter in serving runtime (block pickled payloads) - SEC-948
Rotate/revoke exposed AWS key; enforce pre-commit and CI scrubbing for all test repos - SEC-952
Threat-model changes: default deny egress, KMS policy templates, control-plane bastion for Private customers - SEC-960
Create a provenance + signed-audit workstream (not blocking the above)

Marcos: run kernel compatibility tests for linalg-utils 2.3.1 and report perf delta by 2026-06-18

Priya: draft default KMS policy templates and a Private-control-plane hardening checklist by 2026-06-21 (JIRA:SEC-960)

findings_snapshot:
Open findings prioritized during session:
- F1: linalg-utils deserialization (CVSS ~8.8) — immediate guard, staged upgrade planned. Ticket SEC-948.
- F2: AWS key in redwood-tests (exposed in fixture) — rotated, no evidence of exfil. Ticket SEC-952.
- F3: Private deployment control-plane & KMS posture — design changes needed. Ticket SEC-960.
- Low/Info: minor SCA alerts for 3 transitive deps (tracking in dependency-scan board).
notes_to_self: Keep communication narrow: coordinate kernel/perf testing window with infra maintenance. Avoid mass rollout of dep upgrade until perf sigs are understood. Follow up with legal if any external indicator emerges from rotated key (notify immediately).
